correctness.rationale: Exact Gaussian bridge-gap decomposition proves the finite objective. A positive all-surviving probability implies strict convexity on ordered placements. A singleton-dominance bound scales minimizers as O(1-q), and a uniform third-order expansion yields the unique universal rescaled minimizer. The exact n=2 quadratic has one admissible positive root. A standalone numerical checker recomputed the covariance identities and stationary equations; this is supporting evidence rather than the proof.

Neither result implies the unique posterior-integral Bayes risk optimizer.

value.rationale: A natural robustness question in Gaussian-process quadrature is whether to replicate optimal sensors when independent measurement loss is common. This theorem resolves the all-finite-n small-survival geometry, its sharp microscopic separation coefficient, and the exact two-sensor design. It separates a genuine objective-dependent phase phenomenon from generic sensor-covering intuition; the result is not a numerical table or immediate rescaling of ordinary bridge quadrature.
